title: A From and To date of the transaction day still lists it
steps: Open /transactions
Find the rows: elements whose test id starts with txn-row- inside transactions-table, and wait until there is exactly 1
Read the first row's text and take the first date in MM/DD/YYYY form (pattern \d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4})
Turn that date into YYYY-MM-DD (split on /, then year-month-day); call it the transaction day
Check the transaction day matches YYYY-MM-DD
Type 2099-01-01 into transactions-from
Type 2099-01-31 into transactions-to
Click transactions-apply
Wait for transactions-empty to be visible, because the unfiltered page already shows 1 row, so only a working filter can bring 1 row back from an empty list
Type the transaction day (YYYY-MM-DD) into transactions-from
Type the transaction day (YYYY-MM-DD) into transactions-to
Click transactions-apply

expected.subject: the transaction day converted to YYYY-MM-DD

title: The statement link downloads a PDF for this account
steps: Open /transactions

Wait (web-first) until transactions-statement has an href that matches /api/statements/<customer.checkingId>?year=<4 digits>&month=<1-2 digits>: await expect(link).toHaveAttribute('href', <that regex>). The page fills this link in after it loads (it is '#' at first), so never read it before this wait
Then read the href with getAttribute
Send a GET request to that href as the signed-in page (page.request.get) and read the status and the content-type header

expected.valueFrom: Attribute href ends with /api/statements/<customer.checkingId>?year=<4 digits>&month=<1 or 2 digits> (regex /api/statements/<checkingId>\?year=\d{4}&month=\d{1,2}$)
